note: The q/i shorthand, as data. Written beside a claim's evidence so an agent reads codes rather than prose, and rendered for human readers by docs_hooks/page_metadata.py, which loads THIS file — so the two cannot drift. See CLAUDE.md's Evidence quality tiers / Impact magnitude.

quality.means: Where the study sits on the causal-design ladder: 4 a pre-registered trial or strong meta-analysis, 1 a case study, qualitative study or argument. It answers 'how good is this as evidence of a cause', not 'how well was this study done': a careful interview study is q1 by construction. Read it beside kind and rigour, which judge each study by the standard of what it is. A property of the research, not of whether this page reports it faithfully; that is the separate `verified` axis.

tiers.label: peer-reviewed experiment
tiers.definition: Peer-reviewed experiment (not pre-registered) or systematic review

tiers.label: quasi-experiment
tiers.definition: Quasi-experiment, observational with controls, or narrative review

tiers.label: argument or single case
tiers.definition: Case study, expert opinion, or theoretical argument

kind.means: What sort of evidence the study is. Adopted 2026-09-29 so that rigour can be judged by the standard of the study's own kind.

values.definition: Randomised or quasi-experiment, or single-case design: a manipulated condition and a comparison
Meta-analysis, or systematic review with quantitative pooling
Narrative or scoping review, or a book-length synthesis without a systematic search
Correlational, survey, longitudinal or observational study, with or without statistical controls
Interviews, focus groups, ethnography, case study, thematic or discourse analysis
Design-based research, development or evaluation of an artefact, or a practitioner's report of a design
An argument, model or framework, with or without cited support

rigour.means: How well the study does what its kind can do, judged against that kind's own standard and never another's (criteria in eval/kind-rigor/RUBRIC.md). A rigorous qualitative study is r3; a weak trial is r1.

tiers.label: strong for its kind
tiers.definition: Meets its kind's criteria: e.g. a randomised, powered, low-bias trial; a qualitative study with clear aims, systematic analysis shown and credibility checks

tiers.label: adequate for its kind
tiers.definition: Most of its kind's criteria met, with clear gaps

tiers.label: weak for its kind
tiers.definition: Few of its kind's criteria met: tiny or confounded comparison, thin description, bare assertion

rigour.unknown: r? means the text available (often an abstract) could not show whether the criteria are met; with no text of the study at all, rigour is always r?

impact.means: A legacy bin for a reported statistic, in the study's own terms. These Cohen-like thresholds do not measure educational importance or forecast an individual learner's gain; compare effects only after checking the population and starting state, assignment and comparator, intended outcome and measure alignment, score range and denominator, follow-up time, and uncertainty. For causal K-12 interventions on standardized achievement tests, Kraft (2020) offers a different, empirical reference distribution; do not apply it to every outcome or silently recode these bins. See https://doi.org/10.3102/0013189X20912798.

tiers.label: negligible
tiers.definition: Negligible: an effect size is reported and it is below d 0.2 or equivalent
tiers.history: Until 2026-09-24 this tier read 'negligible or unclear', and the extraction prompt wrote i0 whenever an article printed no effect size. So an i0 written before then may mean either; read the entry's own text. An unreported effect size is now i? (see unknown).

sample.means: Sample size, free text — often a description ('large (multiple course sections)') rather than a number, because a meta-analysis and a classroom study do not count the same thing.

unknown.means: Written but not yet established. `q?` is not the same as an absent q: it says someone looked and could not say, which is a finding rather than a gap.
